sources.title: Sanna Marin: birth and historical ministerial terms
sources.findings: Read official Finnish historical minister record: born 16 November 1985 in Helsinki; transport and communications minister 6 June–10 December 2019; prime minister 10 December 2019–20 June 2023. Exact service dates override abbreviated accounts ending her premiership at the April election. No claim that she is current prime minister or president.

sources.title: Sanna Marin: historical CV as transport and communications minister
sources.findings: Read the short CV hosted by the European Parliament for her transport-minister period: birth, administrative-sciences master’s, MP since 2015, Tampere council chair 2013–2017 and member 2017–2021, regional council 2013–2016. Future/ongoing endpoints in this historical CV are not automatically current. Council chair is not mayor. PDF portrait has only a textual visual description; it was not visually inspected or adopted as a licensed image.

sources.title: Sanna Marin becomes Alumna of the Year: education and public service
sources.findings: Read Tampere University alumni article confirming the 2017 Master of Administrative Sciences from the former University of Tampere and overlap with political service. It calls her the third female Finnish PM and, at appointment at 34, youngest then-serving PM worldwide; the biography uses age without turning a time-specific ranking into a permanent one. Its wording elected to city council in 2013 conflicts with commonly recorded 2012 election/2013 term start; profile only states the securely established 2013–2017 chairmanship. No invented doctorate or full-time exclusive study period.

sources.title: Government of Prime Minister Marin appointed, 10 December 2019
sources.findings: Read 10 December 2019 actual government-appointment release: president appointed Finland’s 76th government and released Rinne ministers; 19 ministers across SDP, Centre, Greens, Left Alliance and Swedish People’s Party. The ordinal counts governments, not unique prime ministers. The biography describes coalition coordination, without treating the cabinet as one-party rule or personal power over every constitutional institution.

sources.title: Government and President declare coronavirus state of emergency, 16 March 2020
sources.findings: Read English version of government release dated 16 March 2020: joint emergency declaration, ordinary/emergency legislative framework, intended decree submission 17 March and planned school changes from 18 March, with exceptions. Final profile and all translations retain prospective wording for the decree and school start rather than claiming implementation proved solely by this advance release. Emergency declaration, submission, parliamentary oversight and measures are separate. No claim all children were barred from education, every restriction began on the 16th, or particular health/economic outcomes were demonstrated.

sources.title: Finland joins NATO as 31st Ally, 4 April 2023
sources.findings: Read NATO’s actual 4 April 2023 accession account: instrument deposited with US government by Foreign Minister Haavisto, President Niinistö present, Finland 31st Ally; allied ratification followed July 2022 protocols. Sweden was still an invitee that day. Membership was not a unilateral act by Marin and she is not invented as the person who deposited the instrument. No quantified security benefit or fastest-ever ranking is adopted from promotional biographies.

sources.title: Parliament accepts Sanna Marin’s resignation as MP, 12 September 2023
sources.findings: Read Yle report of 12 September 2023, 17:28: parliament accepted resignation, effective Wednesday 13 September; she had been re-elected in April. Announcement of plans the prior week is different. Report covers criticism and support, including debate over electoral trust and socially important work. No claim of legal wrongdoing or parliamentary expulsion. Parliamentary search index lists last service day 12 September, consistent with resignation effective next day; direct parliamentary pages had no readable body.

sources.publisher: Tony Blair Institute for Global Change
sources.title: Sanna Marin: current Strategic Counsellor profile
sources.findings: Read current TBI expert page: Strategic Counsellor, joined September 2023, advising political leaders’ reform programmes across the institute’s portfolio. Former premiership and party leadership are distinguished from current advisory work. Promotional climate-target achievements and swiftest-NATO-accession claim are not treated as independently audited outcomes.

sources.publisher: Tony Blair Institute for Global Change
sources.title: Appointment announcement, 7 September 2023
sources.findings: Read TBI press release of 7 September 2023 announcing appointment as Strategic Counsellor. This is the announcement date, distinct from parliament’s 12 September resignation approval and next-day effect. It is not an appointment to the British or Finnish government, nor evidence that every reform advised has succeeded.

sources.title: Hope in Action: publisher record, ISBN 9781668069639
sources.findings: Read Scribner/Simon & Schuster record for ISBN 9781668069639: English Hope in Action: A Memoir About the Courage to Lead, publisher date 4 November 2025, 256 pages. The edition and publisher date are specified rather than inferred from a forthcoming notice or applied to every translation. Read publisher description and metadata, not the whole book. Author photograph credited Elina Simonen was not adopted under an assumed open licence.

sources.title: Sanna Marin’s completed Mulroney Speaker Series conversation, reported 29 October 2026
sources.findings: Read StFX’s 29 October 2026 report describing the completed 27 October Mulroney Speaker Series conversation at Barrick Auditorium. Discussion included uncertainty, Ukraine and women in politics. Report publication and event dates differ. Personal forecasts about war are not factual predictions or Finnish government commitments. This is recent actual-activity evidence; no original event video was watched. A future 26 November Berlin listing is not treated as attendance.

sources.title: North Atlantic Treaty decree and accession procedure, 5 April 2023
sources.findings: Read Finnish government release of 5 April 2023 on the domestic decree. Parliament approved the treaty on 1 March, president decided on accession 23 March; international membership took effect with deposit on 4 April. The 5 April decree completed domestic integration, not a different international accession date. National approval, allied ratification, international deposit and domestic decree are distinguished.
